The polar curve $r=8$ and the ray $\theta =\frac{5\pi }{6}$ intersect at the point $P,$ as shown above. What are the Cartesian coordinates of $P?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The polar coordinates of $P$ are $(r,\theta )=(8,\frac{5\pi }{6}).$ We can convert the polar coordinates of $P$ to Cartesian coordinates, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =8\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{6}) \\  & =8\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =-4\sqrt{3} \\ y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =8\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{6}) \\  & =8\cdot (\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian coordinates of $P$ are $(-4\sqrt{3},4).$
